links.comparator_used: Same device with abstention thresholds loosened to give larger determinate rates, up to 100% (no abstention, always a best-guess output)
links.outcome: PPV, NPV, sensitivity and specificity of determinate outputs versus determinate rate
links.effect: At the selected thresholds, the determinate rate was 63.0% with PPV 92.44%, NPV 97.56%, sensitivity 99.1% and specificity 81.63%. Raising the determinate rate to 81.4% cut indeterminates from 95 to 49, raised false positives from 9 to 22 and false negatives from 1 to 4, and PPV dropped significantly (p=0.039). At 94.7%, PPV and sensitivity dropped significantly (p=0.042). Lowering the determinate rate to 20.9% gave 100% on all four metrics. Raising it to 72.0% significantly improved the determinate rate without a significant accuracy loss.
links.tradeoff: 37% of cases got no determinate output. Stricter thresholds leave fewer children with a result (52.97% would be a significantly lower determinate rate, p=0.047). Of the indeterminate cases, 29.8% had a positive reference-standard autism diagnosis and 88.3% had a noted risk of another neurodevelopmental condition.
links.quote: Restricting determinate outputs to the 63.0% of cases with sufficient certainty prevents the degradation of device performance that is seen when adjusting abstention thresholds to allow for larger determinate rates.

links.comparator_used: Device outputting a positive or negative prediction for more cases, with abstention thresholds loosened toward a 100% determinate rate
links.outcome: Accuracy metrics (PPV, NPV, sensitivity, specificity) and determinate rate across decision thresholds
links.effect: Abstention thresholds that gave a 63.0% determinate rate preserved accuracy (PPV 92.44%, NPV 97.56%). Loosening them to 81.4% significantly dropped PPV (p=0.039) and increased false positives from 9 to 22. Loosening further to 94.7% significantly dropped PPV and sensitivity (p=0.042). Indeterminate cases still received a detailed report and clinician review.
links.tradeoff: 37% abstention rate. Fewer children get a determinate result at stricter thresholds. Indeterminate cases need further clinician evaluation.
links.quote: Restricting determinate outputs to the 63.0% of cases with sufficient certainty prevents the degradation of device performance that is seen when adjusting abstention thresholds to allow for larger determinate rates.
